proposed_comments.title: Prepare query scoring state once before filtering windows
proposed_comments.body:
### Prepare query scoring state once before filtering windows

**Severity:** `medium`

`WindowSearchScorer.Score` is invoked once per window by `FilterListWithScores`, so `query.Split`, `string.Join`, and every `FuzzyStringMatcher.ScoreFuzzy` call repeat for the same query on every keystroke. The new typed/normalized whole-query pass and per-word loop also alternate multiple needles through `FuzzyStringMatcher`'s single prepared-needle cache, so the scorer repeatedly prepares the same query data instead of reusing it as the previous whole-query path did.

Please parse and normalize the query once before iterating the window list, prepare the typed query, normalized query, and word needles once, and pass that immutable scoring state into the per-window scorer. Preserve the current scoring semantics, including the typed-query fallback and the normalized-query maximum. Add or extend a focused test that exercises the reusable state across at least two windows and verifies the same scores as the current implementation. Validate the Window Walker build and focused tests after the change.

findings.claim: Window Walker repeats query parsing and fuzzy-query preparation for every window.
findings.upstream_failure: The exact upstream WindowSearchScorer.Score method is called per window by the filtering path. It splits the query, joins normalized words, scores the typed and normalized whole query, and calls ScoreBothFields for each word inside that method, repeating the work for the same query across all windows.
findings.counterevidence: The current implementation preserves the intended scoring behavior and the exact upstream build passes. That does not remove the repeated hot-path work. The fork-only fix was reviewed by Copilot and returned zero new comments, but its clean review is not used as proof that the upstream tree already contains the fix.
findings.why_not_already_fixed: The upstream head still contains the per-window Score(query, title, processName) API and no reusable scoring-state object is passed from FilterListWithScores.
findings.verification: Source inspection at the pinned upstream head confirmed the repeated operations; the exact upstream Window Walker build passed. The fork-only prepared-state implementation also passed the focused Window Walker build and a fresh Copilot review with zero new published comments. No performance benchmark was run, so the finding is a source-grounded hot-path performance request rather than a measured latency claim.
